# War Scroll Column 15 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all lines in War Scroll Column 15 where the three translators diverged, along with SOPHIA's resolution.

---

## 15:1 — "time of trouble" vs. "time of distress" vs. "hour of crisis" — eschatological designation

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "time of-trouble" | Literal rendering of 'et tsarah |
| LOGOS | "time of distress" | Formal rendering echoing Daniel 12:1 |
| PNEUMA | "hour of crisis" | Dynamic rendering for urgency |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "time of distress" (LOGOS). Echoes Daniel 12:1 (the likely source text); "hour of crisis" (PNEUMA) imports a contemporary register inappropriate for prophetic/apocalyptic language.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 15:1 — "appointed time of war" vs. "appointed time of battle" vs. "appointed time for war"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "appointed-time of-war" | Literal construct |
| LOGOS | "appointed time of battle" | "battle" as alternative to "war" |
| PNEUMA | "appointed time for war" | Changed preposition for English flow |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "appointed time of war" (EMET). milchamah is "war" (the broader conflict), not just a single "battle."

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET with LOGOS formatting.

---

## 15:2 — "great panic" vs. "great terror" vs. "great terror" — eschatological fear

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "great panic" | Rendering of mehumah rabbah |
| LOGOS | "great terror" | Formal rendering |
| PNEUMA | "great terror" | Same as LOGOS |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "great terror" (LOGOS/PNEUMA). mehumah can mean "panic/confusion/terror"; "terror" better captures the eschatological gravity.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS/PNEUMA.

---

## 15:2-3 — "sons of Japheth" vs. "descendants of Japheth" — Genesis 10 reference

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "sons of-Japheth" | Literal rendering of beney Yephet |
| LOGOS | "sons of Japheth" | Standard biblical rendering |
| PNEUMA | "descendants of Japheth" | Modern equivalent |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "sons of Japheth" (EMET/LOGOS). This is a biblical designation from the Table of Nations (Genesis 10); "sons" is the standard rendering of beney in ethnic designations.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 15:3 — "dominion of the Kittim" vs. "empire of the Kittim" — political terminology

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "dominion of-the-Kittim" | Literal rendering of memshelet |
| LOGOS | "dominion of the Kittim" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "empire of the Kittim" | Interprets as Roman Empire |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "dominion of the Kittim" (EMET/LOGOS). memshelet means "dominion/rule"; "empire" is a historically specific interpretation (identifying Kittim as Romans).

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 15:4 — "Sons of Darkness" vs. "those who belong to darkness" — community designation

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "Sons of-Darkness" | Standard sectarian designation |
| LOGOS | "Sons of Darkness" | Same, capitalized |
| PNEUMA | "those who belong to darkness" | Dynamic paraphrase |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "Sons of Darkness" (EMET/LOGOS). This is a technical self-designation of the Qumran community's enemies; paraphrasing loses the term's specificity.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 15:5 — "Sons of Righteousness" vs. "Those who belong to righteousness" — parallel designation

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "Sons of-Righteousness" | Sectarian designation |
| LOGOS | "Sons of Righteousness" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "Those who belong to righteousness" | Dynamic paraphrase |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "Sons of Righteousness" (EMET/LOGOS). Same reasoning as Sons of Light/Darkness; these are technical designations.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 15:6 — "appointed times of darkness" vs. "seasons of darkness" vs. "every last season of darkness"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "appointed-times of-darkness" | Literal rendering of mo'adey choshekh |
| LOGOS | "seasons of darkness" | mo'adim as "seasons" |
| PNEUMA | "every last season of darkness" | Expanded for emphasis |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "appointed times of darkness" (EMET). mo'adim in DSS contexts specifically means "appointed times" (divinely ordained periods), not merely "seasons."

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 15:6 — "exalted greatness" vs. "supreme majesty" — divine attribute

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "His-exalted-greatness" | Literal rendering |
| LOGOS | "His exalted greatness" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "His supreme majesty" | Dynamic rendering |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "His exalted greatness" (EMET/LOGOS). "Supreme majesty" imports regal language not present in the Hebrew.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 15:8 — "fierce destruction" vs. "terrible carnage" vs. "fierce and devastating battle"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "fierce-destruction" | Literal rendering |
| LOGOS | "terrible carnage" | Heightened register |
| PNEUMA | "fierce and devastating battle" | Expanded description |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "fierce destruction" (EMET). Concise and literal; "terrible carnage" (LOGOS) is slightly purple; PNEUMA's expansion adds unnecessary words.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 15:9-10 — "congregation of the angels and the assembly of men" vs. "heaven's army and the human forces"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "congregation of-the-angels and-the-assembly of-men" | Literal parallel structure |
| LOGOS | "congregation of the angels and the assembly of mortals" | "mortals" for contrast with angels |
| PNEUMA | "heaven's army and the human forces" | Military language |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "congregation of the angels and the assembly of men" (EMET base, LOGOS format). The paired nouns "congregation/assembly" (edah/qahal) are technical Qumran terms. LOGOS's "mortals" adds connotation; PNEUMA loses the communal terminology.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 15:11 — "shouting of a great multitude" vs. "roar of a great multitude" vs. "thunderous roar of a vast army"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "shouting of-a-great-multitude" | Literal rendering |
| LOGOS | "roar of a great multitude" | "Roar" for collective sound |
| PNEUMA | "thunderous roar of a vast army" | Added "thunderous" and changed "multitude" to "army" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "roar of a great multitude" (LOGOS). "Roar" better captures the collective battle sound than "shouting"; PNEUMA's additions are unwarranted.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 15:12 — "tribulation" vs. "agony" — eschatological suffering term

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "tri[bulation]" | Standard apocalyptic term with lacuna |
| LOGOS | "tri[bulation]" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "agony" | Dynamic rendering without lacuna marking |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "tri[bulation]" (EMET/LOGOS). The lacuna is genuine and must be marked; "tribulation" is the standard eschatological term.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 15:14-15 — "lots" vs. "rounds" — battle structure terminology

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "three lots" | Literal rendering of goralot |
| LOGOS | "three lots" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "three times" / "three rounds" | Interprets "lots" as battle rounds |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "three lots" (EMET/LOGOS). goral means "lot" (as in casting lots); the term carries theological weight about divine destiny, not merely sequential rounds.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 15:15 — "strengthen himself" vs. "gird himself" vs. "rally" — Belial's action

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "shall-strengthen-himself" | Literal rendering of yitchazeq |
| LOGOS | "shall gird himself" | Military metaphor |
| PNEUMA | "will rally" | Modern military term |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "shall strengthen himself" (EMET). yitchazeq (Hitpael of chzq) literally means "strengthen oneself"; "gird" (LOGOS) is a different Hebrew root; "rally" (PNEUMA) is too modern.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 15:16 — "infantry battalions" vs. "foot soldiers" — military unit terminology

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "infantry-battalions" | Rendering of gedudey raglim |
| LOGOS | "infantry battalions" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "foot soldiers" | Simplified rendering |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "infantry battalions" (EMET/LOGOS). gedudim are organized military units ("battalions"), not individual soldiers.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 15:17 — "the great hand of God" vs. "God's mighty hand" — divine intervention

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the-great-hand of-God" | Literal construct chain |
| LOGOS | "the great hand of God" | Same, unhyphenated |
| PNEUMA | "God's mighty hand" | Possessive with interpretive adjective |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "the great hand of God" (EMET/LOGOS). The Hebrew uses gedolah ("great"), not gibburah ("mighty"); PNEUMA substitutes the adjective.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

**Total disagreements:** 17
